references.title: DWDS: gerade
references.supports: No Wortzerlegung; the Adverb entry ('betont die Exaktheit einer Angabe: genau'), apart from the two Adjektiv entries

references.title: en.wiktionary: gerade
references.supports: Etymology 1 (the adverb senses): 'equivalent to ge- + the root of Rad'

notes.rationale: gerade das, was die Männer einen 'Scharm' nennen, precisely that: DWDS's Adverb, so ADV (ADR 0054); geradezu's gold description 🎯 fits it too. en.wiktionary's 'equivalent to ge- + the root of Rad' analyses the Old High German girat, not a modern German surface: no modern part spells 'rade'. So under the 2026-10-27 dictionary rule (ADR 0054) neither dictionary splits it, as with gold Bad and Bauer (#1241 round 9, settled). DWDS gives no Wortzerlegung, so it is a bottom word, and indeclinable, so it has no Ending, not even ∅ (ADR 0051): the Root gerade alone.
